text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi says a constitutional review will be done only after the general election (expected next year) and that it must involve the majority of Kenyans.
- Rival Somali faction leaders Hussein Aideed and Ali Mahdi Mohamed arrive in Nairobi for exploratory peace talks which are to be hosted by Kenya's President Moi.

- A former vice-chairman of the giant Kenya Co-operative Creameries and son of Kenya's president, Raymond Moi, denies attending a meeting on the takeover of the milk company. He says has no interest in buying or taking over firm.

- Diversey Eastern and Central Africa Ltd and Lever Industrial Division of East Africa Industries merge to form DiverseyLever following an announcement a few months ago that the Unilever Group was acquiring Diversey Corporation worldwide.

- Kenya's Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister Kalonzo Musyoka discloses that African United Nations member states have vowed to re-elect U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros Ghali for a second term.
- A middle-aged man gets a rude shock when he is stripped by a furious woman thought to be a prostitute.
- Minister Kalonzo Musyoka says that the United Nations owes Kenya 1.2 billion shillings ($20 million) for peacekeeping missions and services.
- Opposition party FORD-Asili officials reject the Opposition Alliance that calls for a single presidential candidate saying it is a move to manipulate the next general election.

- A multi-billion money-minting scam is in the making under a suspicious motor vehicle licensing and traffic control project between the Ministry of Transport and Communications and a dubious London-based company which is said to enjoy political backing from a clique of ruling KANU party politicians.

- Giant grower body Kenya Planters Cooperative Union (KPCU) says coffee production is in dire need of a shot in the arm having declined from 130,000 tonnes in 1987/88 to 73,000 tonnes in the 1992/93 season and will offer farmers cheap off-shore loan facilities to enable them to rehabilitate coffee trees.
